summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and a gastrostomy tube was admitted to the surgery service for observation after a home accident in which she stepped on and tugged her feeding tube, leading to three days of abdominal pain, increased yellow cloudy drainage, and square-shaped erythema around the dressing. She was kept NPO with tube feeds held, given IV fluids and pain control, and underwent a G-tube contrast study showing the tube tip in the stomach with contrast passing into the small bowel and no extraluminal leak. Tube feeds were restarted and tolerated without nausea or vomiting, and the skin irritation improved with frequent dressing changes; pain persisted mainly at granulation tissue at the tube site but was controlled on oral medication. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with instructions for ongoing dressing care, PRN pain medication, and surgical follow-up in two weeks for possible tube repositioning if symptoms persist.
problems: Other specified procedures as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
